subject.title: Add an FxTwitter read transport for public lookups, threads, profiles, and search

question: Should Birdclaw core own an explicitly selected FxTwitter/FxEmbed read transport, including its privacy disclosure, endpoint trust policy, capability boundary, and third-party reliability obligations?
rationale: The existing architecture can host the adapter, but source inspection and repository vision cannot determine whether the project intends to support this public external service as a core transport.

options.title: Approve a bounded experimental adapter
options.body: Add an opt-in core transport with no automatic fallback, a narrow public-read capability set, strict endpoint validation, canonical persistence, and explicit privacy/status reporting.

options.title: Defer pending transport policy
options.body: Keep the proposal open but postpone implementation until Birdclaw defines a general policy for public and self-hosted HTTP acquisition transports.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Document that Birdclaw supports only its existing live transports unless a future external-adapter interface can host FxTwitter outside core.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded experimental adapter
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in core transport with no automatic fallback, a narrow public-read capability set, strict endpoint validation, canonical persistence, and explicit privacy/status reporting.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes Birdclaw’s product boundary and ongoing support obligations, and the current vision/history identifies steipete as the strongest available decision owner.
